text:
alex: FYI I'm bringing Orion-21B (Gemma-origin) into the llama-serving path. Conversion + int4 quant runs OK on short benches but long-context QA shows repetition and occasional sentence fractures after ~2k tokens.

rachel: can you paste the minimal repro and the convert/quant flags?

alex: minimal steps below. conversion uses gemma->llama auto-mapping; quantize uses int4 with pack-order=interleave. Served on dedicated dev nodes.

```bash
python convert_gemma_to_llama.py --in orion21b.gemma --out orion21b.llama --autodetect-head-layout
python quantize.py --model orion21b.llama --dtype int4 --calib 200000 --pack-order interleave
redwood serve --model orion21b.int4 --profile long-qa
```

dmitri: paste a failing example? the "sentence fractures" part sounds like phase misalignment or token mapping drift.

alex: example (trimmed):

float32: "...the committee advised a staged migration over three quarters, focusing on low-risk namespaces."
int4:   "...the committee advised a staged migration over three quarters, focusing on low-risk namesp
Fragment: ensure to verify tokens.
"

alex: it's inserting a fragment mid-token boundary. CI/fact-eval shows drop in BLEU/BERTScore on long-qa set. Short answers unaffected.

rachel: did you run a quant-sim (fake int) to see if packing order alone reproduces it?

alex: yes. fake-quant with interleave packing reproduces. Switching to contiguous-head packing in sim removes the issue.

dmitri: that implies serialization/layout mismatch between packer and runtime application of rotary frequency tables. Common root: when packer interleaves head blocks but runtime expects contiguous heads, phase swaps happen for grouped dims and produce garbled KV cache for long contexts.

ops-bot: artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-dev/model-artifacts/orion21b/pack-debug/ (sha256: 9f8c4b2e).

rachel: run a per-head max-diff diagnostic: compare orig rotary base to deserialized under both pack orders and print heads with large diffs. small snippet: 

```py
for h in range(num_heads):
    diff = np.max(np.abs(base_orig[h] - base_loaded[h]))
    if diff > 1e-7: print(h, diff)
```

alex: ran it: diffs concentrated on head groups [6,7,14,15,22,23]. matches interleaved pairs.

dmitri: remediation options: (1) make packer default to runtime-canonical (contiguous-head) layout and re-pack artifacts, (2) emit header metadata with head_layout and a small checksum/CRC for rotary tables so runtime can validate and remap, (3) add a conversion smoke test to CI that checks rotary alignment.

rachel: option 2 is lowest-risk short-term. add header and runtime validator to avoid silent regressions. Option 1 for long-term to simplify. Also add the per-head alignment smoke to conversion CI.

alex: opening RI-2099 with artifacts and a proposed patch to write head_layout + crc32 in the converted bin. I'll tag eng-runtime for runtime-side checksum validation.

ci-bot: build 2304 triggered: tests/convert::orion-head-layout-check started.

ops-bot: scheduled an overnight long-qa eval on repacked int4 artifact if CI passes.

dmitri: once we have a green run, plan a small migration to repack any models converted in the last 30 days. Also coordinate a note to customers if their private converted models are in that window.

alex: thanks all. marking for follow-up after CI + overnight eval. :spiral_calendar:
